answer: One concrete defense is costly staking bonds: each agent must lock scarce collateral to act, so spinning up a meadow of fake identities stops being free. Like felling timber, every new seat demands real resource expenditure, and slashing burns the bond of any identity caught colluding. The ledger signs each action with the agents own quill, tying reputation to staked value, so cloning identities multiplies cost without multiplying trust and sybil swarms become economically irrational.
